text:
alex: FYI — AcmeCorp (dedicated) opened a config request asking for customer-scoped batching limits. They want token_budget=1500 and max_queue=8 per pool. They say p99 needs to be <500ms for chat flows.

maya: Got the ticket. They sent a sample workload and say KV cache hit is ~40% and avg seq len ~120 tokens. They want a config preview before we push to prod. :+1:

jamal: Current global defaults are token_budget=1024, max_queue=32, and continuous-batching seeds off sequence-length histograms. That token_budget bump seems reasonable but reducing max_queue from 32->8 could increase tail latency if bursts come in.

rachel: We should profile the queue policy change. If we lower max_queue per-customer, we may need to tighten admission control to prevent head-of-line blocking across pools. Also watch KV cache eviction behavior when token_budget grows.

alex: Agreed. Can we run a quick sim on the load shape they provided? I can drop their histogram into the perf harness.

jamal: I'll run the simulator. Quick note: our batching heuristic chooses batch formation up to min(remaining_token_budget, batch_token_cap) with a soft deadline of 25ms queue wait. If we set token_budget=1500, batch_token_cap needs to increase or we'll underutilize the budget.

maya: They prefer explicit limits rather than heuristics. Could we expose two knobs: token_budget and max_queue, and keep the soft_deadline policy internal? They want tenant-level SLA controls.

rachel: That's doable. Expose knobs but keep runtime safety guards: global_max_queue_sum and per-host concurrency caps. We should add telemetry flags to track per-tenant queue length, avg queue wait, and batch size distribution.

alex: Sample config snippet they proposed: 
```json
{
  "customer": "acme-corp",
  "token_budget": 1500,
  "max_queue": 8,
  "burst_policy": "allow_burst"
}
```
Does that look safe to test in staging?

jamal: Staging ok if we cap burst_policy to a staging-safe value. I'll run the sim with their workload and the staging safety net (global_max_queue_sum=256, host_concurrency=64).

rachel: For profiling, enable KV cache trace for one shard. We need to verify increased token_budget doesn't cause cache thrash (we saw regressions before when budget jumped). Add a perf counter for kv.evictions_per_minute and kv.hit_ratio_by_prefix.

alex: Perfect. Can you post the sim results here when ready? I'll then prepare the config change request to support-team for dedicated rollout.

deploy-bot: Simulation job 87342 queued by jamal. ETA ~7m. Logs: https://ci.internal/sim/87342

maya: Thanks all — once we have sim+kv traces we'll share the recommended safe defaults to Acme and propose a 2-week canary on Dedicated pool A.

jamal: Simulation finished. Quick summary: with token_budget=1500 & max_queue=8 the average latency stays ~220ms, p99 ~480ms for their trace, batch sizes grew from 6->9 tokens avg, kv.hit_ratio stable at 39% (down 1.2 pts). No obvious thrash but evictions increased ~8%. I'll upload full logs and flamegraphs.

rachel: Good data. Increase kv cache size for their pool by 10% in canary to offset evictions, and enable eviction backpressure so heavy workloads degrade gracefully.

alex: I'll draft the dedicated config request: include token_budget=1500, max_queue=8, kv_cache_delta=+10%, staging_canary=true, telemetry_flags for batch_size & kv metrics.

maya: Sounds good. I'll sync with the customer on the canary window and get their sign-off. :handshake:
